verdict.rationale: Sentry's Trace Explorer and Issues page let developers filter/aggregate by arbitrary properties like impacted users, browser, or device with 'flexible queries and filters' without needing pre-defined dashboards or indexes (sentry-docs-9, sentry-docs-10, sentry-docs-36). This implies ad-hoc high-cardinality filtering (e.g. user id) is supported, but the evidence never explicitly addresses request-id-level grouping, cardinality limits, or performance at scale. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of high-cardinality tag/attribute indexing behavior, request-id grouping examples, and independent/hands-on confirmation of performance with high-cardinality fields.
